사람.forms: 사람이 · 사람을 · honorific: 분 · plural: 사람들
사람.x: There are so many people in the park.
사람.e: Add it to a country for nationality: 한국 사람 (Korean), 미국 사람 (American).

과일.e: Probably from older 과실 (fruit) — its 과 likely the same 'fruit' as in 사과.

보다.m: to see, to look at, to watch; to take (an exam)
보다.x: I watched a movie in the evening.
보다.t: After a verb, -아/어 보다 means 'try doing': 먹어 보세요 = try eating it. 시험을 보다 = take a test.

보다.forms: same after consonant or vowel · A보다 B가 더 … (B is more … than A)
보다.e: Comes from 보다 (to see). 커피보다 차 = tea rather than coffee.
보다.t: As a particle it attaches directly to a noun.

보다.forms: 보다 + adjective/adverb (보다 나은, 보다 많이); spoken ≈ 더
보다.ex: 우리는 보다 나은 미래를 위해 노력합니다.
보다.x: We work hard for a better future.
보다.e: Same form as the particle -보다 'than'; here it stands alone before the word.
보다.t: Formal, written style; in speech say 더: 더 나은 미래.

열다.forms: 열어요 · 열었어요 · 열 거예요 · 여세요 (ㄹ drops)
열다.x: It's hot. Please open the window.
열다.t: ㄹ drops before ㅅ, ㄴ, ㅂ: 여세요, 여는 시간 (opening time).

모두.forms: 모두 + verb: 모두 왔어요 · also a noun: 모두가
모두.x: All the students came to the classroom.
모두.e: Also a noun: 모두 = everyone. 여러분 모두 = all of you.

하고.forms: same after consonant or vowel: 빵하고 우유 · (누구)하고 같이 (with someone)
하고.x: I watched a movie with my friend.
하고.e: From 하다 + -고. The everyday spoken 'and/with': 친구하고 영화 봐요.
하고.t: Easy to use: one form for every noun, no batchim rule.

할인.x: Students can get a 10 percent discount.
할인.e: Literally 'cut and pull' the price down.
할인.t: Pronounced [하린]. Use 할인을 받다 for "get a discount" and 할인해 주다 for "give a discount."

주차하다.x: Excuse me, where can I park my car?

건너가다.x: When the light changes, cross the street at the crosswalk.
건너가다.e: 건너다 'to cross' plus 가다 'to go': cross over, away from the speaker.

올라오다.m: to come up, to come upstairs; to come up to Seoul
올라오다.x: Take the elevator up to the third floor now.
올라오다.e: 오르다 (to climb) + 오다 (to come): come up toward the speaker.
올라오다.t: Koreans say 서울에 올라오다 for traveling to Seoul from anywhere else, no matter the direction on a map.

기침.ex: 감기 때문에 밤에 기침이 계속 나요.
기침.x: Because of my cold, I keep coughing at night.
기침.e: Used with 나다 or 하다: 기침이 나다 (a cough comes), 기침을 하다 (to cough).

수술.ex: 할아버지의 수술이 잘 끝나서 가족들이 기뻐했어요.
수술.x: Grandpa's surgery went well, so the family was happy.
수술.t: Patients 수술을 받다, 'receive surgery,' while doctors 수술하다, 'operate.'

연주하다.m: to play (a musical instrument), to perform (music)
연주하다.ex: 제 동생은 피아노를 아주 잘 연주해요.
연주하다.x: My younger sibling plays the piano really well.
연주하다.t: In daily speech, 치다 is used for piano and guitar, 불다 for wind instruments; 연주하다 works for all.

파리.ex: 파리에 가면 에펠탑을 꼭 보고 싶어요.
파리.x: If I go to Paris, I really want to see the Eiffel Tower.
파리.e: From French 'Paris'. Homonym warning: native 파리 also means 'fly' (the insect).

발표.x: I gave a presentation in Korean in class.

애인.ex: 실례지만 혹시 지금 만나는 애인 있어요?
애인.x: Excuse me, but are you seeing anyone right now?
애인.t: Gender-neutral and common, unlike English 'lover'; it doesn't suggest an affair.

서로.x: Our family lives helping one another.
서로.e: Also works as a noun: 서로의 생각 'each other's thoughts'.

담다.m: to put in, to fill (a container); to contain
담다.ex: 남은 음식을 그릇에 담아서 냉장고에 넣었어요.
담다.x: I put the leftover food in a bowl and put it in the fridge.
담다.e: Sounds just like 닮다 'resemble'; context tells them apart.

단점.ex: 제 단점은 성격이 너무 급하다는 거예요.
단점.x: My weakness is that I'm too impatient.
단점.e: Literally 'short point', where you fall short.

현금 인출기.ex: 이 근처에 현금 인출기가 어디 있어요?
현금 인출기.t: In daily conversation most Koreans simply say ATM (에이티엠).

사회.e: Literally 'community gathering.' Homonym 사회 means hosting or emceeing an event.
사회.t: 사회생활 usually means life in the working world, not your social life.

차분하다.ex: 언니는 성격이 차분해서 화를 잘 안 내요.
차분하다.x: My older sister has a calm personality, so she rarely gets angry.
차분하다.e: Describes a quiet, settled nature; also used for calm colors or atmosphere.
차분하다.t: 차분하다 is a calm personality or mood; 침착하다 is staying cool in a crisis.

식습관.x: I changed my eating habits for my health.

부하.ex: 김 부장님은 부하 직원들에게 항상 친절해요.
부하.x: Manager Kim is always kind to the employees under him.
부하.t: 부하 can sound hierarchical; in polite office talk people often say 후배 or 팀원 instead.

야근.ex: 이번 주에는 야근이 많아서 너무 피곤해요.
야근.x: I've had to work late a lot this week, so I'm really tired.

관람하다.m: to watch, to view (a show, game or exhibition)
관람하다.x: I watched a musical with my family.
관람하다.t: Pronounced [괄람하다]: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ.

열매.m: fruit (of a plant), berry; result, fruits (of effort)
열매.ex: 가을이 되면 나무에 열매가 많이 열려요.
열매.x: In the fall, lots of fruit grows on the trees.
열매.e: Related to 열리다 'to bear fruit': 열매가 열리다 is the natural pairing.
열매.t: 열매 is fruit on any plant; 과일 is fruit you buy and eat. 노력의 열매 = the fruits of effort.

멀어지다.m: to grow apart, to drift apart; to become distant, to get farther away
멀어지다.ex: 졸업 후에 그 친구와 점점 멀어졌어요.
멀어지다.x: After graduation, that friend and I gradually drifted apart.

제한.ex: 이 수영장은 나이 제한이 있어서 어린이는 못 들어가요.
제한.x: This pool has an age limit, so children can't go in.
제한.t: Common compounds: 시간 제한 'time limit', 나이 제한 'age limit', 속도 제한 'speed limit'.

개최.ex: 다음 달 서울에서 국제 영화제가 개최될 예정입니다.
개최.x: An international film festival is scheduled to be held in Seoul next month.
개최.t: News style: N이 개최되다 'N is held'; in speech, people say 열리다.

안정적.x: Many people want a stable job.

화분.x: I watered the potted plant on the balcony.
화분.t: 화분 means both the pot and the plant in it: 화분을 키우다 'grow a potted plant'. A potted plant is a classic housewarming or shop-opening gift.

창업자.ex: 이 회사의 창업자는 대학생 때 사업을 시작했어요.
창업자.x: This company's founder started the business as a college student.

파견.ex: 그는 일 년 동안 베트남 지사에 파견을 갔어요.
파견.x: He was sent to the Vietnam branch for a year.

칼럼.ex: 저는 매주 그 교수님의 칼럼을 읽어요.
칼럼.x: I read that professor's column every week.
칼럼.e: From English 'column', newspaper sense only; a pillar is 기둥.

소셜 미디어.ex: 저는 소셜 미디어에 사진을 자주 올려요.
소셜 미디어.x: I often post photos on social media.
소셜 미디어.t: In everyday speech Koreans usually say SNS [에스엔에스] rather than 소셜 미디어.

목격자.ex: 경찰이 그 사고의 목격자를 찾고 있어요.
목격자.x: The police are looking for witnesses to the accident.
목격자.e: Literally 'a person whose eyes were struck' by the event.
목격자.t: 목격자 is someone who saw the event; 증인 is someone who testifies in court.

진화.ex: 소방관들이 두 시간 만에 불을 진화했습니다.
진화.x: Firefighters put out the fire in two hours.
진화.e: Literally 'subduing the fire'; don't confuse with the homonym 진화 'evolution.'
진화.t: 진화 is news language (화재가 진화됐다); in everyday speech say 불을 끄다.

필기시험.x: I passed the written driver's license test on the first try.

지휘.ex: 오늘 공연은 유명한 지휘자가 지휘를 맡았어요.
지휘.x: A famous conductor led today's performance.
지휘.e: Literally 'point and wave', like a conductor's baton.
지휘.t: Also used outside music: 경찰의 지휘 아래 'under police command'.

과학적.x: This method has been scientifically proven.
과학적.e: -적 = '-ic, -al', turning nouns into descriptions: 과학적, 혁신적, 이론적.
과학적.t: Use -적인 before nouns (과학적인 방법) and -적으로 as an adverb (과학적으로 설명하다).

천연가스.x: These days many buses run on natural gas.

유언.ex: 할머니는 가족들에게 사이좋게 지내라는 유언을 남기셨어요.
유언.x: Grandma's last words to the family were to get along with each other.
유언.t: Collocation: 유언을 남기다 = to leave a will or last words.

기쁨.ex: 아이의 웃음은 우리 가족에게 큰 기쁨이에요.
기쁨.x: Our child's laughter is a great joy to our family.

미움.ex: 그는 거짓말 때문에 친구들에게 미움을 받았어요.
미움.x: He was disliked by his friends because of his lies.

못마땅하다.x: My grandmother disapproved of my short hair.
못마땅하다.e: 못 'not' + 마땅하다 'proper, suitable' — something doesn't seem right to you.
못마땅하다.t: Pronounced [몬마땅하다]; for a third person's feeling, use 못마땅해하다.

끈기.ex: 그는 끈기가 있어서 쉽게 포기하지 않아요.
끈기.x: He's tenacious, so he doesn't give up easily.
끈기.e: Literally 'sticky energy' — related to 끈끈하다 'sticky'; you stick with things.

감히.forms: 감히 + verb (감히 말하다); 감히 어디서! = How dare you!
감히.m: dare to, venture to; how dare
감히.ex: 저는 감히 선생님께 반대 의견을 말할 수 없었어요.
감히.x: I didn't dare to voice a different opinion to my teacher.
감히.e: Sino syllable 'dare, be bold' plus adverb ending -히.
감히.t: 감히 말씀드리면 is a humble way to say 'if I may be so bold'; 감히! alone scolds someone.

감시하다.m: to watch, to monitor, to keep under surveillance
감시하다.x: The police are keeping the suspect under 24-hour surveillance.

머리를 맞대다.forms: 머리를 맞대요 · 머리를 맞댔어요 · 머리를 맞대고 + verb
머리를 맞대다.m: to put heads together, to brainstorm together
머리를 맞대다.x: The team members put their heads together and solved the problem.
머리를 맞대다.e: 맞대다 = to put face to face; picture heads touching over a problem.
머리를 맞대다.t: Pronounced [맏때다]: the batchim makes the following ㄷ tense.

변수.ex: 날씨가 이번 경기의 가장 큰 변수예요.
변수.x: The weather is the biggest wild card in this game.
변수.e: Literally 'changing number', from math; now any unpredictable factor.
변수.t: Pronounced [변쑤]; in news, 변수 often means a factor that could change the outcome.

원동력.x: My family is the driving force behind my hard work.
원동력.e: Literally 'original moving power': what keeps you going.

차원.ex: 이 문제는 국가 차원에서 해결해야 해요.
차원.x: This problem has to be solved at the national level.
차원.e: Used both for space (3차원 '3-D') and for the level at which something is handled.

수선.x: The pants were too long, so I took them in for alteration.
수선.t: 수선 is mainly for clothes, shoes and bags; for machines and buildings, use 수리.

손금.e: 손 'hand' + 금 'line, crease' (as in 금이 가다 'to crack').
손금.t: Pronounced [손끔]: ㄱ becomes tense in this compound. 'To read palms' is 손금을 보다.

조차.forms: Same form after any noun: 이름조차 · 물조차 · (+ usually a negative)
조차.x: I was so busy I couldn't even eat lunch.
조차.e: Native particle that points to the most basic thing you'd expect — and says even that didn't happen.
조차.t: Mostly with negatives or bad situations: 이름조차 몰라요 'I don't even know the name.' For a positive 'even', use 도 or 까지.

치고.forms: Same form after any noun: 겨울치고(는) · 외국인치고(는) · N치고 … 없다 (every N)
치고.m: for a …, considering it's …; (with a negative) every … without exception
치고.e: From the verb 치다 'to count as, regard as' + -고: 'counting it as a …'.
치고.t: Two uses: 겨울치고(는) 따뜻해요 'warm for winter'; with a negative it means 'every': 부모치고 자식 걱정 안 하는 사람은 없어요 'There's no parent who doesn't worry about their kids.'

자금.ex: 회사는 연구 자금을 마련하기 위해 투자자를 찾고 있어요.
자금.x: The company is looking for investors to raise research funds.
자금.t: Collocation: 자금을 마련하다 or 자금을 조달하다 (raise funds).

재벌.ex: 한국 경제에서 재벌의 영향력은 여전히 큽니다.
재벌.x: The chaebol still have great influence on the Korean economy.
재벌.e: Literally 'wealth clan'; English borrowed the word as 'chaebol'.

오보.x: The broadcaster officially apologized for the false report.

표제.m: headline, title (of an article or book)
표제.x: A big headline ran on the front page of the newspaper.
표제.t: 표제 is formal; in everyday speech people say 제목 or 헤드라인.

환경친화적.ex: 정부는 환경친화적 에너지 정책을 추진하고 있습니다.
환경친화적.x: The government is pushing an eco-friendly energy policy.
환경친화적.t: In everyday speech the shorter 친환경 is far more common: 친환경 제품 'eco-friendly products'.

창작물.ex: 다른 사람의 창작물을 허락 없이 사용하면 안 돼요.
창작물.x: You shouldn't use other people's creative work without permission.
창작물.t: Pronounced [창장물] — ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㅁ (nasalization).

무산되다.m: to fall through, to come to nothing
무산되다.ex: 예산 부족으로 그 계획은 결국 무산되었습니다.
무산되다.x: The plan eventually fell through due to a lack of funds.
무산되다.e: Literally 'scatter like fog' — plans vanishing into thin air.

소멸하다.m: to die out, to disappear, to expire
소멸하다.ex: 인구가 줄면서 소멸할 위기에 놓인 지방 도시가 늘고 있어요.
소멸하다.x: As the population shrinks, more provincial towns are at risk of dying out.
소멸하다.t: Also used for expiring rights or points: 포인트가 소멸되다 'points expire.'

기피하다.m: to avoid, to shun, to evade (a duty)
기피하다.ex: 요즘 젊은이들은 힘든 일을 기피하는 경향이 있어요.
기피하다.x: These days young people tend to avoid hard jobs.
기피하다.e: Literally 'dread and avoid' — shunning something you dislike.
기피하다.t: Common collocations: 병역 기피 'draft dodging' and 기피 대상 'someone or something people avoid'.

허다하다.x: There are a great many people who make this kind of mistake.
허다하다.e: Means 'a great many'; mostly in phrases like 허다한 경우 'countless cases'.
허다하다.t: Often says something happens all the time: 그런 일은 허다해요.

조마조마.x: My heart was pounding nervously as I waited for the results to be announced.
조마조마.e: A doubled mimetic word; the repetition mirrors a heart fluttering with worry.
rel: to be on pins and needles

약육강식.m: survival of the fittest, the law of the jungle
약육강식.ex: 자연은 강한 동물이 살아남는 약육강식의 세계입니다.
약육강식.x: Nature is a dog-eat-dog world where strong animals survive.
약육강식.e: Literally 'the weak are meat, the strong eat'.

특목고.m: special-purpose high school (e.g., science or foreign-language high school)
특목고.ex: 제 동생은 과학고 같은 특목고에 가고 싶어 해요.
특목고.x: My younger sibling wants to go to a special-purpose high school like a science high school.
특목고.e: Short for 특수 목적 고등학교, 'special-purpose high school'.
특목고.t: Pronounced [틍목꼬] — nasalization of ㄱ before ㅁ.

나열하다.m: to list, to enumerate, to line up
나열하다.x: Try listing the pros and cons one by one.

현금흐름.x: Sales went up, but cash flow isn't good.
현금흐름.e: 현금 'cash' + native 흐름 'flow,' from 흐르다 'to flow.'

친서.m: personal letter (from a head of state)
친서.ex: 대통령은 특사를 통해 상대국 정상에게 친서를 전달했습니다.
친서.x: The president delivered a personal letter to the other country's leader through a special envoy.

편저.m: compiled and written work, edited volume
편저.ex: 이 책은 김 교수의 편저로 출판되었습니다.
편저.x: This book was published as a volume compiled and written by Professor Kim.
편저.e: Literally 'compile and write' — partly the editor's own writing, partly collected material.

주마간산.m: skimming superficially, looking at things in a rush
주마간산.x: I didn't have time, so I just rushed through the museum.
주마간산.e: Literally 'viewing mountains from a galloping horse'.

수렴되다.m: to be gathered, to be incorporated (opinions); to converge
수렴되다.ex: 시민들의 의견이 새 정책에 충분히 수렴되었습니다.
수렴되다.x: Citizens' opinions were fully incorporated into the new policy.
수렴되다.t: Active 의견을 수렴하다 'to collect opinions' is very common; in math, 수렴 means 'convergence'.

조야하다.m: coarse, crude, unrefined (of manners or style)
조야하다.x: His way of speaking was coarse, but his heart was warm.
조야하다.t: 조악하다 describes poor-quality goods; 조야하다 describes unrefined manners or style.

페미니즘.x: Debates about feminism are heated online.

삼림.ex: 울창한 삼림이 산 전체를 덮고 있어요.
삼림.x: Dense forest covers the whole mountain.
삼림.e: Literally 'dense trees and woods'; both syllables picture trees.
삼림.t: Pronounced [삼님]: ㄹ after ㅁ turns into ㄴ.

고사하다.m: to decline firmly, to turn down politely
고사하다.x: He ultimately declined the offer of a minister's post.
고사하다.e: Literally 'firmly decline': refusing an honor or offer, usually out of modesty.
고사하다.t: Homonyms: 고사하다 can also mean 'to wither' (枯死); -는 고사하고 means 'let alone.'

소외하다.m: to alienate, to exclude, to leave out
소외하다.ex: 우리 사회가 노인들을 소외하고 있지는 않은지 생각해 봐야 합니다.
소외하다.x: We need to consider whether our society is leaving the elderly out.
소외하다.t: The passive 소외되다 and noun 소외감 are much more common than 소외하다.

부대끼다.m: to be jostled, to rub shoulders with; to be harassed, to be troubled; (stomach) to feel unsettled
부대끼다.ex: 출근길 지하철에서 사람들에게 부대껴서 너무 피곤해요.
부대끼다.x: I'm exhausted from being jostled by people on the subway to work.
부대끼다.e: Pictures bodies bumping against each other in a crowd.

단아하다.ex: 그녀는 단아한 한복 차림으로 손님들을 맞았어요.
단아하다.x: She welcomed the guests dressed in an elegant hanbok.

천연스레.m: nonchalantly, as if nothing happened, naturally
천연스레.x: Even after lying, he smiled as if nothing had happened.

호사다마.m: good things come with many obstacles
호사다마.x: They say good things come with hitches — it rained on our wedding day.
호사다마.t: Often quoted as 호사다마라고 or 호사다마라더니 when trouble interrupts something happy.
